title: Cost-Efficient Large Language Model Serving for Multi-turn Conversations with CachedAttention
technique: hierarchical (DRAM/SSD) KV cache store reused across conversation turns, with layer-wise preloading, async saving, scheduler-aware fetch/eviction and decoupled positional encoding

optimized_metrics.evidence: CachedAttention significantly decreases the time to the first token (TTFT) by up to 87%
reduces the end-to-end inference cost by up to 70%
improves the prompt prefilling throughput by up to 7.8x for multi-turn conversations
CachedAttention enables the saved KV caches to remain valid via decoupling the positional encoding and effectively truncating the KV caches

headline_claim.text: CachedAttention significantly decreases the time to the first token (TTFT) by up to 87%, improves the prompt prefilling throughput by up to 7.8x for multi-turn conversations, and reduces the end-to-end inference cost by up to 70%.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: TTFT is an important metric for quality of service in LLM serving. It indicates how quickly users start seeing the output of LLMs after entering their prompt.
metric_definitions.notes: mean not stated; under Poisson arrivals so queueing may be included but is not discussed

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Prefilling throughput is the metric to evaluate the speed of processing the prompt.
We evaluate the resource cost based on the on-demand price of AWS EC2 instances, i.e., $5/hour per A100 GPU, $0.0088/hour/GB for DRAM and $0.000082/hour/GB for SSD.
metric_definitions.notes: GPU time plus DRAM/SSD storage cost

load_regime: Poisson session arrivals (lambda=1.0 sessions/s) over 9K ShareGPT conversations; also varied session arrival rate sweep (§4.3.8)
hardware: A100 GPUs, DRAM and SSD (up to 10TB) tier
extractor_notes: Title and abstract frame the goal as cost; TTFT is the primary latency metric. Cache hit rate is the internal driver (eviction policy) but treated as reported intermediate.
